prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The starting network learned to press DONE at once (episode length 1.0, success 0), so no evidence about architectures exists yet. The traces show a key clue: the target heights the agent observes are the design cyclically shifted by 4 = X/2 columns in x (row 1: 00220000 shows as 00000022; row 6: 00000010 shows as 00100000; the same shift fits all rows of design 2). Rewards and actions use world coordinates. A 2-layer 3x3 CNN (receptive field ±2) cannot match the target to the build or the actions across a 4-column shift, so every placement looks random and costly, and DONE is the rational choice. The fixes are to align the frames: (A) feed the network copies of the channels both unshifted and shifted by X/2, or (B) a learned circular 1xX convolution that can learn any x-shift. (C) adds a cheaper recipe with more updates and more entropy to fix (A).

### Round 2
The starting network was misaligned: the observed target is shifted by X/2 columns, and every placement looked wrong to it, so it learned to press DONE at once. Feeding the network the observation next to a copy rolled by X/2 fixed this (r1c1: 0.59, seeds 0.48 and 0.70). A learned 1xX circular convolution also learned the shift but scored lower (0.35). The lean recipe (2 PPO epochs, 128 environments, ent 0.02) learned much faster on seed 0 (0.65 dev, 0.59 train) but its other seed failed completely (0.0). So more samples look valuable, but the small batch was unstable. Under the default recipe, training success was still rising steeply at the end, so the agent is short of samples. The traces show the agent pressing DONE too early with target cells still missing (design 1), and trouble with stacked or overhanging columns. Both point to weak global and ordering reasoning.

### Round 3
The observed target is shifted by X/2 columns in x. Adding a rolled copy of the input (dual-frame) fixes this: success went from 0 to 0.59. Cutting PPO epochs from 4 to 2 while keeping 256 envs nearly doubled the samples, and success rose to 0.79 (seeds 0.78 and 0.80), the clearest gain beyond noise so far. Training success was still rising steeply at the end (0.39 to 0.71 over the last half), so the agent is short of samples. Two additions to r2c1 scored much lower: a dilated third conv (0.11) and a global broadcast (0.24). Both mostly failed by choosing DONE too early with the upper layers still missing. Seed spread is large (up to 0.3), but neither result is close. Extra capacity or extra paths have not helped yet. The best bets are recipe changes: more samples (1 epoch), and a longer reward horizon so the +1 exact-build bonus reaches early ordering choices and discourages early DONE.

### Round 4
The observed target is shifted by X/2 in x. Adding a rolled copy of the input (dual-frame) fixes this: dev success went from 0 to 0.59. The learned circular row conv also worked but scored lower (0.35). Cutting PPO epochs from 4 to 2 at 256 envs gave the best result so far (r2c1, 0.79, both seeds close). Most failures look like seeds collapsing to DONE-only. That happened with 1 epoch (0.21/0.00), with gamma 0.99 (0.00/0.32 and 0.00/0.00), and in one seed with 128 envs. The sign is consistent: a longer horizon makes it look worse to keep placing randomly than to stop, and more frequent noisy updates lock in that choice. The two architecture additions (dilated conv, global broadcast) scored lower, partly through fewer samples and partly through seed luck. For the last round, I keep the r2c1 network and recipe and change one thing per trial to make collapse less likely: shorter horizon, more entropy, or near-uniform output initialisation.

## Trial it ended with
name: r2c1 with gamma 0.9
hypothesis: Only change from r2c1: gamma goes from 0.95 to 0.9. Gamma 0.99 made seeds collapse to DONE because random early placements add up to a large negative return. A shorter horizon makes stopping early look less attractive, while each correct cell still pays straight away. The exact-build bonus is paid at the DONE step itself, so it is not discounted. Expect a mean above 0.79 with no collapsed seed. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.79.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
